source: user-led triage discussion from the Notion improvement-registry evidence
pinned_impl_ssot_commit_note: Self-reference is impossible: this file and the AMEND-F amendment to tpch-sspq/IMPL-SSOT.md are recorded in a single commit, so that commit's SHA cannot be embedded in this file. The amended IMPL-SSOT is identified instead by pinned_impl_ssot_blob below, which is exactly the blob SHA every worker verifies under IMPL-SSOT section 1-d. The commit SHA is reported in the commit message and in the agent report.

benefit_adjustments.refutes: full removal of the 62.35% profile band
benefit_adjustments.ranking_treatment: no numeric benefit score, no rank position until resolved; excluded from the percentile-rank population
benefit_adjustments.note: expected_saved_seconds multiplies fresh_base_median_q, a wall-clock median, by the effect fraction. If the 13% is a CPU-time reduction, applying it to a wall median overstates the benefit, potentially by a large factor because the candidate's target work is parallelisable. Blocked on exactly one datum: whether the prototype's 13% is a wall-time or a CPU-time reduction. Resolvable by the user; not a rejection.

benefit_adjustments.ranking_treatment: no numeric benefit score, no rank position; contributes 0 seconds to any campaign-level total
benefit_adjustments.independent_existing_reason: feasibility-assessment.json already assigns IMP-002 the deferred_research lane because CUBRID has no BufferAccessStrategy equivalent
benefit_adjustments.note: The two reasons are independent and BOTH stand. The deferred_research lane is a feasibility judgment; BENEFIT_CONFOUNDED is an evidence judgment. Neither subsumes the other, and lifting one does not lift the other.

benefit_adjustments.discovery_priority_action: NOT MODIFIED — the registry's and Notion's discovery Priority field is left exactly as it is
benefit_adjustments.ranking_treatment: score from the 0.138 s projection at the Projection evidence weight 0.50, per IMPL-SSOT section 2-b
benefit_adjustments.note: The absolute magnitude of 0.138 s does not support a P0 discovery priority. This is recorded as a disagreement in the campaign's own fields only; the discovery-side Priority is a different question (how interesting the finding is) from the campaign-side rank (how much wall time an implementation would buy), and this campaign does not overwrite the former.

benefit_adjustments.ranking_treatment: compute expected_saved_seconds from the 0.47 core-s realistic target only
benefit_adjustments.note: Direct application of the IMPL-SSOT section 2-b rules: a whole profile band is never automatically a removable effect, and a range contributes its conservative lower bound. The 32.7% band is a cost observation, not an effect.

lane_status_changes.note: This removes IMP-025 from the ranked performance set. It is an ownership change, not a benefit judgment.

upstream_scope_gates.mapping_note: The triage stated these upstream references as a SET applying to this SET of candidates. It did NOT state which ticket applies to which candidate. No per-candidate mapping is recorded, because inventing one would fabricate specificity the triage did not supply. Each gated candidate is therefore checked against ALL six references.
upstream_scope_gates.rule: Before any implementation work begins on a gated candidate — before the first source edit and before its implementation-plan.md is complete — its scope MUST be checked against every reference listed here, and the result recorded in that candidate's implementation-plan.md. If the upstream work already covers the candidate's scope, that is a stop-and-report condition (IMPL-SSOT section 11-a), not a reason to proceed in parallel.

evidence_confirmed_sound_note: The direct A/B evidence for these six candidates was examined in the triage and found without defect. This is a POSITIVE finding: it raises confidence in these candidates' benefit inputs and MUST be visible in each one's ranking rationale, not merely absent from the defect list. It does not change any evidence weight — direct A/B is already 1.00 — it confirms that the 1.00 is earned.

preserved_tensions.tension: IMP-011 and IMP-014 appear in BOTH the upstream scope-gate set and the evidence-confirmed-sound set.
preserved_tensions.resolution: NOT RESOLVED — both hold simultaneously, by design. Sound A/B evidence establishes that the cost is real; it does not establish that the fix is still this campaign's to write. Sound evidence does NOT exempt a candidate from the upstream scope check.

preserved_tensions.tension: IMP-002 carries two independent negative findings: the deferred_research lane in feasibility-assessment.json (no CUBRID BufferAccessStrategy equivalent) and BENEFIT_CONFOUNDED here (Q04 attribution confounded with IMP-018).
preserved_tensions.resolution: NOT RESOLVED into one reason — both are recorded and both stand independently.

preserved_tensions.tension: IMP-012 is P0 in the discovery-side improvement registry, but its campaign-side absolute effect is a 0.138 s projection.
preserved_tensions.resolution: NOT RESOLVED by overwriting either side. The registry/Notion Priority field is untouched; the disagreement lives only in this campaign's fields.

contradictions_with_pinned_inputs.detail: IMP-025 is lane 'performance' there; this triage moves it to external_tracking. IMP-028 and IMP-007 are lane 'deferred_research' there; this triage moves them to external_tracking. IMP-011 is lane 'deferred_research' there, yet it is gated for upstream scope-check and its evidence was confirmed sound here — those are not lane statements and do not by themselves promote it.
contradictions_with_pinned_inputs.handling: feasibility-assessment.json is NOT modified (IMPL-SSOT section 2-b-1 keeps it immutable). The lane changes are recorded here as the later, higher-authority input and the ranking tool applies them; the divergence is stated rather than silently reconciled.

contradictions_with_pinned_inputs.detail: IMP-012 priority P0 and IMP-028 priority P0 are unchanged in the registry while this campaign de-queues IMP-028 and disputes the P0 magnitude basis of IMP-012.
contradictions_with_pinned_inputs.handling: The registry is INPUT EVIDENCE ONLY (IMPL-SSOT section 1-b) and is not modified. The disagreement is recorded here only.

open_questions.question: Is the internal prototype's ≈13% measured effect a WALL-TIME reduction or a CPU-TIME reduction?
open_questions.why_it_matters: expected_saved_seconds multiplies a wall-clock median (fresh_base_median_q); a CPU-side fraction applied to a wall median overstates the benefit, and the overstatement is large precisely because the target work is parallelisable.
open_questions.until_answered: IMP-001 stays BENEFIT_PENDING_DENOMINATOR with no benefit score and no rank position

open_questions.question: After IMP-018 and IMP-010 are fixed, should IMP-002's Q04 attribution be re-measured, or does its deferred_research lane make re-measurement moot for this campaign?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The confound and the lane are independent; clearing the confound does not by itself make IMP-002 implementable here.

open_questions.question: Is there a per-candidate mapping between the six upstream references (CBRD-27127, CBRD-27036, CBRD-27037, CBRD-27094, CBRD-27113, PR #7453) and the five gated candidates?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The triage supplied the references as a set. Recorded as set-to-set; each gated candidate is checked against all six, which is safe but more work. A per-candidate mapping, if one exists, would narrow the gate.

open_questions.question: Who owns tracking PR #7533 and CBRD-26788 to resolution, and where is that tracking state recorded once this campaign closes?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The external_tracking lane definition (IMPL-SSOT section 4-a) requires tracking to a resolution, but this campaign's closeout (section 11-b) has no step that discharges it.
